steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Strong melodies have clear phrase structure — typically 4-bar or 8-bar phrases with a sense of question (antecedent) and answer (consequent). | Key Fact: Develop melodies through: sequence (repeating at a different pitch), inversion (turning upside down), augmentation (stretching), fragmentation (using part of the idea). | Key Fact: Match rhythm to genre: rock riffs use syncopation and repetition; Classical melodies use balanced phrasing; jazz melodies use swing and blue notes. | Key Fact: Staff notation requirements: you must submit a score in staff notation (up to 4 sharps/flats) — notation quality affects the AO2 mark for technical control.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how melody writing are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use melody writing. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use melody writing in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
